title: Read notes through MCP by Portable path

intentCoverage.report:
**Verdict: Caught.** Maintained proof catches this fault on the real SDK ambiguity → candidate selection → full-read journey.

**Next proof action:** Retain the existing SDK recovery scenario in MCP verification. This probe supports no assertion repair for this fault; broader coverage decisions remain with the caller.

Story: `SEED-125#read-notes-through-mcp-by-portable-path`, source `.planning/seeds/SEED-125-read-notes-through-mcp-by-portable-path.md#read-notes-through-mcp-by-portable-path`, completed plan `092-read-notes-through-mcp-by-portable-path/PLAN.md`. Checked revision: `ff63ab95acb61440011f76081ac49f9ed988078d`, branch `codex/read-notes-through-mcp-by-portable-path`. Verified the supplied dedicated linked worktree at that revision with clean tracked/untracked Git status before probing. Its configured isolated database and `http://127.0.0.1:61139` origin were selected by every run.

The selected promise is that an ambiguous read returns actual readable folder candidates whose selected Portable path resolves to the intended full note. The maintained scenario is `AI agent recovers an ambiguous read by selecting a returned path` in `e2e_test/features/mcp/mcp_services.feature:73`. Its two `Engineering` notes share the title `Code Review`, under `Practices/Design` and `Other/Design`. It reads `Engineering:Code Review`, selects the returned `Practices/Design` candidate, passes that candidate's path unchanged, and checks the resulting address and full folder trail.

Introduced exactly one temporary production fault: added `.structuredContent(result)` to the ambiguity result builder at `backend/src/main/java/com/odde/donut/mcp/McpNoteLookup.java:79`. The existing `isError`, candidate text, matching, fixtures, and assertions stayed intact. The result map contains `message` and `candidates`, while the discovered successful read output schema requires full-note fields.

Reach and wrong behavior were observed through the maintained client, not inferred from the edited line. `mcp_client.ts:50` calls the actual SDK's `listTools`, caching output validators. The faulted journey then failed at `cy.task('callMcpToolWithParams')` with MCP error `-32602`: structured content failed the output schema because `portablePath`, `title`, `notebookName`, `folderPath`, and `updatedAt` were missing. The runtime stack identifies SDK 1.32.2 `Client.callTool` (`src/client/index.ts:747`), `McpClient.callMcpToolWithParams` (`mcp_client.ts:77`), and the task adapter (`mcpClientTasks.ts:27`). Inspection confirmed that the SDK validates present structured content even on an error result. Thus the ambiguous response was rejected before the assistant could obtain candidates and select a returned address.

The actual catcher was this earlier SDK output-schema validation, propagated by `mcpAgentActions.callTool:91` from `readNoteAfterSelectingAmbiguousCandidate:119`. Its rejection fails the maintained scenario. The later candidate-existence and selected-read location assertions were not reached in the faulted run. Baseline and restored passes exercised those later assertions successfully.

All three phases used the same command:

`CURSOR_DEV=true nix develop -c env SUT_TIMEOUT_MS=360000 pnpm cy:run --spec e2e_test/features/mcp/mcp_services.feature`

- Baseline: exit 0; 8 passed, including the selected journey.
- Faulted: exit 1; 7 passed and only the selected recovery journey failed. Its configured Cypress retry also failed with the same schema rejection; no additional manual fault run was launched.
- Restored: exit 0; 8 passed, including the selected journey.

Ran one owned heavy invocation at a time on this 16-CPU host. Fresh launch load readings were 37.94, 40.59, and 48.21; inspected memory readings showed no throttled pages. Kept the supplied supported 360-second health timeout and left unrelated processes alone.

A signal-aware `finally` guard restored the saved original source bytes immediately after the fault run. Final comparison matched the pre-probe revision, branch, status, unstaged diff, staged diff, stash identities, and source SHA-256 (`06c55f03031b9a7dc8b55c94515eb496a78f043f3ee65138ca715e1a1b2f3645`). All three command processes exited; owned SUT ports 61137–61139 had no listeners. No probe commit, staging, test edit, or fixture edit remains. Logs, the one-line patch, pre-probe manifest, and restoration evidence are retained outside the repository in `/tmp/seed125-intent-coverage-1794486216366/`; the decisive runtime failure is in `fault.log:57–80`.

This matches the already-settled slice 6 / obligation G5 disposition: actual cached-schema SDK recovery proof was added for this caller behavior. It confirms that existing disposition rather than creating a new repair decision. The finding is limited to the observed two-folder ambiguous read and this SDK path.

- **Test runtime.** 141 seconds total (measured from Cypress Results: baseline 46 s, faulted 45 s, restored 50 s). Separately, complete command durations including Nix, stack startup, and cleanup were 217.168 s, 134.871 s, and 162.872 s, totaling 514.911 s (measured with the host monotonic clock).
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no separately supported human-effort measurement was supplied or observed.
- **Agent effort.** Approximately 5 agent-minutes (estimated active source review, scratch setup, evidence analysis, restoration verification, and report preparation; excludes runner waiting; no active-time telemetry).


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 740128 ms (measured), from 1794486216366 to 1794486956494 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.


Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision: ff63ab95acb61440011f76081ac49f9ed988078d. Accepted Caught for the observed two-folder ambiguity and actual cached-schema SDK path only. The existing maintained recovery scenario catches the deliberate fault before candidate selection; no delivered defect or assertion gap was found. Retain that scenario; no test repair, new correction or follow-up queue item is required. This confirms the existing slice6/G5 disposition and does not claim protection for every story promise. Parent inspected fault.log57–80, the three terminal JSON results and complete restoration evidence, including matching source SHA-256 and clean revision/branch/index/worktree. No product change followed the check. Product-review no-change advice remains settled.
